subject: Cost & unit-econ checks for MAP: tokens, caching & batching
messages:
From: Emma Soto <emma.soto@acmehealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cost + unit econ checks for MAP

Hi Avery,

Thanks for sending over the MAP last week. Procurement and our ML infra team asked for a focused unit-econ sanity check before we lock dates for the pilot. High-level ask: can Redwood validate the tokens/$ and operational assumptions in the MAP (caching, batching, warmup overhead) and give a realistic cost range for a 30-day pilot and a subsequent production ramp (1M monthly inference calls)?

Quick context:
- Typical request: short clinical note -> summary + suggested coding. Average observed input tokens ~350, average model output ~900 (we've measured variability).
- Expected traffic shape: 1M monthly calls, but bursty (peak 8k qps for short windows).
- Latency requirement: p95 < 400ms.
- We plan to use the MAP canary + dedicated pool if unit economics look right.

Attached is our current MAP (MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) and a sample token profile. Can you and your team:
1) Confirm reasonable tokens-per-call assumptions and recommended caching/hit-rate for prefix matches
2) Provide an estimate of tokens/$ under hosted vs dedicated (rough order of magnitude) and any batching wins we should expect
3) Call out warmup/kv-cache overhead and any recommended trial instrumentation (what to measure in week-1 canary)

Would love a short readout tomorrow afternoon if possible — procurement is pushing a week deadline.

Best,
Emma
Emma Soto
Head of Data Products, Acme Health

Attachments: MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); sample-token-profile.csv
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Soto <emma.soto@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost + unit econ checks for MAP

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the MAP draft. High-level: we can run a quick simulation + tabletop audit today and share conservative + optimistic bands by late afternoon. Proposed approach:

- Quick sim inputs (what we'll use): avg tokens/call = 1,250 (350 in, 900 out), cache-hit assumptions: optimistic 50% (for heavy prefix reuse), conservative 30% for billing/sales rooms; batching effects: avg batch size 3–4 during normal loads (peak batching lower).
- Baseline unit-cost (hosted): ~ $0.0045 per 1k tokens (readout estimation for rw-infer-13B on multi-tenant). Dedicated pool delta: expected 35–50% lower per-token cost at sustained volume depending on quantization and reserved capacity.
- Operational overheads: KV cache population (~1–3 tokens/call equivalent for control), warmup (first 10–20 requests after scale-up incur cold overhead), alignment/extra-retries ~2–4% requests.

I'll attach a quick token profile CSV (acme_token_profile.csv) with the sim. Laura / Neha — can you run smoke-check numbers against the MAP assumptions and flag anything we should be conservative about?

I can do a 20–30m readout today at 3:30pm PT.

Thanks,
Avery
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_token_profile.csv
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost + unit econ checks for MAP

On Tue, Jul 11, 2028 at 10:05 AM Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> - Quick sim inputs (what we'll use): avg tokens/call = 1,250 (350 in, 900 out), cache-hit assumptions: optimistic 50% (for heavy prefix reuse), conservative 30% for billing/sales rooms; batching effects: avg batch size 3–4 during normal loads (peak batching lower).

Avery — quick notes from a commercial and ops perspective:
- I agree we should present both bands, but for procurement use the conservative cache hit (30%). Marketing/execs love optimistic numbers; procurement will expect us to defend the conservative case.
- Add a separate line-item for KV-cache prefetch cost: if Acme prefetches 10% of common prefixes during onboarding there is GPU time + egress cost to consider (treat as one-time amortized across the pilot).
- Batching: don't promise 4x efficiency. For median traffic and the 8k burst windows we should model batching wins as 10–20% (not 30+) unless they commit to queueing.
- Latency SLO hit: plan for a canary on dedicated pool for the first 7 days and an SRE checklist to measure p50/p95/p99 token-latency split. If p95 > 400ms at target throughput, trigger fallback to a smaller model variant.

I'll try to join the 3:30 readout.

—Laura
Director, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost + unit econ checks for MAP

Quick simulation summary (ran against acme_token_profile.csv & traffic shape):
- Sim inputs used: 1,200 tokens/call avg (conservative); cache-hit = 30% (conservative); average batch size = 3.2 -> estimated batching efficiency = 18% lower per-token CPU-time; extra alignment/warmup overhead 5% added.
- Resulting tokens-per-1k-calls: (1,200 tokens/call * 1,000 calls) = 1,200,000 tokens.
- Effective billed tokens after caching & batching = ~820,000 tokens (this assumes we can apply batching before billing where applicable; some hosts bill raw tokens — call that out).
- Cost bands: hosted estimate = $0.0045 per 1k tokens -> $3,690 (hosted conservative band) for 1M calls/month; dedicated (reserved) estimate ~= 40% lower -> ~$2,214/month equivalent (plus reserved capacity fee amortized).
- Recommendation: present procurement a two-line ask: 1) scoped pilot credits for hosted (cover 4 weeks at hosted conservative cost) + 2) commitment threshold (e.g., 300k calls/mo) to flip to reserved pricing with a ramp. Also add a 30% contingency buffer in the MAP for unexpected tail tokens and latency-related retries.

I've dropped a simulation workbook to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcMEtokenSim (unit_econ_v1.xlsx attached). Please review and flag any modeling differences we should surface to Acme.

- Neha
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: unit_econ_v1.xlsx
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Soto <emma.soto@acmehealth.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost + unit econ checks for MAP — assumptions & next steps

Emma / procurement — thanks for the quick turn. Below is a succinct summary of what we agreed internally and what we'll put in the MAP document for procurement review. We'll attach the simulation workbook and the MAP appendix with line-item assumptions.

Agreed conservative assumptions (to include in MAP):
- Avg tokens/call: 1,200 (350 input / ~850 output)
- Conservative cache hit-rate: 30% (prefix reuse); optimistic band: 50%
- Effective batching efficiency: ~18% (avg batch size ~3.2)
- Warmup & alignment overhead: 5% token-equivalent reserve
- Hosted estimate (conservative): $0.0045 per 1k tokens -> ~$3,690 / month for 1M calls
- Dedicated (reserved) estimate: ~40% lower per-token unit cost at sustained volume -> ~$2,214 / month equivalent (plus contract/reserved fee)
- Contingency: 30% buffer recommended in procurement ask to cover tail risks and retries

Operational asks / canary plan:
- Week-0: instrumentation plan (token-level telemetry, KV-hit metric, p50/p95/p99 latency) — Neha will share a dashboard template.
- Week-1 (canary): run on dedicated pool for 7 days, monitor p95 < 400ms at target throughput; fallback policy to smaller model variant if not met.
- Canary start target: Aug 1st, 2028.

Next steps (owner):
- I will update the MAP appendix with the conservative bands + attach unit_econ_v1.xlsx (Avery).
- Neha to share dashboard link and simulation workbook (Neha).
- Laura to own procurement messaging and the reserved capacity ask (Laura).
- Emma / Acme to confirm canary start date and whether they want an initial prefetch window for KV population.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-4521
Drive simulation: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcMEtokenSim

Thanks — I'll circulate the updated MAP v2 by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (updated MAP v2 to follow), acme_token_profile.csv, unit_econ_v1.xlsx
